Work with H3 directed edges

Source: R/h3_edge.R
ddbh3_edge.Rd

Create H3 directed edges from H3 cells, and convert H3 directed edges to cells, lengths and spatial lines. A directed edge goes from an origin cell to one of its neighbors (the destination cell)

Usage

ddbh3_h3_to_edge(
  x,
  h3start = "h3string",
  h3end,
  new_column = "h3edge",
  conn = NULL,
  name = NULL,
  mode = NULL,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  quiet = FALSE
)

ddbh3_h3_to_edges(
  x,
  h3 = "h3string",
  new_column = "h3edge",
  nested = FALSE,
  conn = NULL,
  name = NULL,
  mode = NULL,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  quiet = FALSE
)

ddbh3_edge_to_origin(
  x,
  h3edge = "h3edge",
  new_column = "h3origin",
  conn = NULL,
  name = NULL,
  mode = NULL,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  quiet = FALSE
)

ddbh3_edge_to_destination(
  x,
  h3edge = "h3edge",
  new_column = "h3destination",
  conn = NULL,
  name = NULL,
  mode = NULL,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  quiet = FALSE
)

ddbh3_edge_to_h3(
  x,
  h3edge = "h3edge",
  new_column = "h3cells",
  nested = FALSE,
  conn = NULL,
  name = NULL,
  mode = NULL,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  quiet = FALSE
)

ddbh3_reverse_edge(
  x,
  h3edge = "h3edge",
  new_column = "h3edge_reversed",
  conn = NULL,
  name = NULL,
  mode = NULL,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  quiet = FALSE
)

ddbh3_get_edge_length(
  x,
  h3edge = "h3edge",
  unit = "m",
  new_column = "edge_length",
  conn = NULL,
  name = NULL,
  mode = NULL,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  quiet = FALSE
)

ddbh3_edge_to_spatial(
  x,
  h3edge = "h3edge",
  conn = NULL,
  name = NULL,
  mode = NULL,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  quiet = FALSE
)

Arguments

x

Input data. One of:

duckspatial_df

A lazy spatial data frame via dbplyr.

sf

A spatial data frame.

tbl_lazy

A lazy data frame from dbplyr.

data.frame

A standard R data frame.

character string

A table or view name in conn.

character vector

A vector of values to operate on in vectorized mode (requires conn = NULL).

h3start

The name of a column in x containing the H3 strings or H3 unsigned 64-bit integers (UBIGINT). The path starts on this cell

h3end

The name of a column in x containing the H3 strings or H3 unsigned 64-bit integers (UBIGINT). It's the destination cell of the path

new_column

Name of the new column to create on the input data. If NULL, the function will return a vector with the result. If the input already has a column with this name, it is replaced by the result

conn

A connection object to a DuckDB database. If NULL, the function runs on a temporary DuckDB database.

name

A character string of length one specifying the name of the table, or a character string of length two specifying the schema and table names. If NULL (the default), the function returns the result as an sf object

mode

Character. Controls the return type. Options:

  • "duckspatial" (default): Lazy spatial data frame backed by dbplyr/DuckDB

  • "sf": Eagerly collected sf object (uses memory)

Can be set globally via ddbs_options(mode = "...") or per-function via this argument. Per-function overrides global setting. It only applies when the output has a geometry column, and is ignored otherwise.

overwrite

Boolean. whether to overwrite the existing table if it exists. Defaults to FALSE. This argument is ignored when name is NULL.

quiet

A logical value. If TRUE, suppresses any informational messages. Defaults to FALSE.

h3

The name of a column in x containing the H3 strings or H3 unsigned 64-bit integers (UBIGINT)

nested

Logical. If TRUE, children are returned as a nested list column (one row per parent cell). If FALSE (default), the result is unnested so each child cell occupies its own row.

h3edge

Name of the column containing H3 directed edge indexes, as strings or unsigned 64-bit integers (UBIGINT). Defaults to "h3edge"

unit

Character. Unit of the edge length. One of "m" (default), "km" or "rads". Only used in ddbh3_get_edge_length().

Value

One of the following, depending on the inputs:

tbl_lazy

If the output has no geometry, i.e. x is not spatial and the function adds a column. mode is ignored in this case.

duckspatial_df

If the output has geometry (x is spatial, e.g. an sf or duckspatial_df object, or the function builds geometries, as *_to_spatial() and ddbh3_h3_to_points() do) and mode = "duckspatial" (default).

sf

If the output has geometry and mode = "sf".

TRUE (invisibly)

If name is provided, a table is created in the connection and TRUE is returned invisibly.

vector

If x is a character vector and conn = NULL, the function operates in vectorized mode, returning a vector of the same length as x.

Details

The functions cover the full directed edge workflow:

  • ddbh3_h3_to_edge() returns the directed edge going from the cell in h3start to the cell in h3end. It returns NA when the cells are not neighbors

  • ddbh3_h3_to_edges() returns all directed edges going out of an H3 cell (6 for hexagons, 5 for pentagons) — either nested (one row per cell) or unnested (one row per edge) depending on nested

  • ddbh3_edge_to_origin() returns the origin cell of a directed edge

  • ddbh3_edge_to_destination() returns the destination cell of a directed edge

  • ddbh3_edge_to_h3() returns both the origin and the destination cells of a directed edge — either nested (one row per edge) or unnested (one row per cell) depending on nested

  • ddbh3_reverse_edge() returns the directed edge going in the opposite direction (from destination to origin)

  • ddbh3_get_edge_length() returns the length of a directed edge in unit

  • ddbh3_edge_to_spatial() converts directed edges to LINESTRING geometries (EPSG:4326) shared by the origin and destination cells

Directed edges are returned in the same format as the input cells: strings for H3 strings and UBIGINT for H3 unsigned 64-bit integers.

Examples

## Load needed packages
library(duckh3)
library(dplyr)

## Setup the default connection with h3 and spatial extensions
## This is a mandatory step to use duckh3 functions
ddbh3_default_conn(threads = 1)

## Load example data
points_tbl <- read.csv(
  system.file("extdata/example_pts.csv", package = "duckh3")
)

## Add h3 strings
points_tbl <- ddbh3_lonlat_to_h3(points_tbl, resolution = 8)

## CELLS TO EDGES ---------

## All edges going out of each cell (one row per edge)
edges_tbl <- ddbh3_h3_to_edges(points_tbl)

## All edges going out of each cell (one row per cell)
ddbh3_h3_to_edges(points_tbl, nested = TRUE)

## Edge between two neighboring cells
pair_tbl <- data.frame(
  h3start = "8a1fb46622dffff",
  h3end   = "8a1fb46622d7fff"
)
ddbh3_h3_to_edge(pair_tbl, h3start = "h3start", h3end = "h3end")
#> # A query:  ?? x 3
#> # Database: DuckDB 2.0.1 [unknown@Linux 7.0.0-1020-azure:R 4.6.2/:memory:]

## EDGES TO CELLS ---------

## Origin and destination cells

  ddbh3_edge_to_origin() |>
  ddbh3_edge_to_destination()
